proof.command: cd packages/dispatch && DISPATCH_E2E_REUSE_SERVERS=1 DATABASE_URL='postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:5433/dispatch_tester?sslmode=disable' FAKE_ENVOY_PORT=9121 FAKE_GITHUB_PORT=9122 FAKE_BROKER_PORT=9124 DISPATCH_E2E_PORT=8877 PLAIN_HTTP_PORT=31820 PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/legion/scratch/tmp/ms-playwright bunx playwright test --config e2e/playwright.config.ts --project=chromium e2e/conversation.e2e.ts -g 'passage'. Then a throwaway spec (removed) with five editor cases
proof.observed: 3 passed, including 'the editor keeps a cited passage's id when its whole text is typed over' (b1, b2 'Other words entirely.', b3; the reply reads b2 removed:false). In the throwaway spec: a Backspace join after an emoji keeps b1 and reads b2 removed. A cut paragraph pasted twice keeps b2 on the first paste, and select-all then retype sends blocks [] and reads b2 removed. Typing over b2 and undoing back to the original sends b1, b2 and b3 and keeps b2. Typing over b2 together with its paragraph break joins it to b3, so b2 is kept on 'New Gamma.' and b3 is removed. That is R11's join rule, and the server's text rules give the same result without ids. Typing over two whole blocks at once sends neither id, and the reply reads b2 removed
proof.negativeControl: Typing over two whole blocks at once ('Merged.') sends only b1 and gives a new b4, so the citation reads removed:true. The fix keeps an id only when one block's whole text is typed over
